proof_note: Krawczyk inclusion: K(X) subset int(X), where after realifying w in C^4 to x in R^8, K(X) = x_0 - Y F(x_0) + (I - Y DF(X))(X - x_0) with F = F_tilde_R, X = x_0 + [-rho, rho]^8, and Y approximately DF(x_0)^{-1}. If sup_{J in DF(X)} ||I - Y J||_inf < 1 with Y invertible, then every J in DF(X) is invertible (Neumann series). Hence the root certified inside X is nondegenerate. The recorded contraction_bound is sqrt(2) times an upper bound on sup_{J in DF(X)} ||I - Y J||_inf. Each mesh point has a local Krawczyk box; this is NOT an interval-in-gamma certificate unless certificate_type is gamma_interval_tube. These certificates prove local uniqueness in the listed seed boxes/tubes. They do not prove global uniqueness, absence of external saddles, thimble dominance, or the QAOA exponent. Competitor certificates outside the seed boxes do not contradict this theorem. Phi_eff is evaluated at the Newton/Krawczyk center (numerical); the certified root lies in X_gamma. Residual and box_radius are recorded.

certificate_summary.action_note: An interval enclosure of Phi(w_*(gamma)) is obtained by evaluating Phi_eff over the certified box X_gamma with the log(Delta_star) branch fixed by continuation along the mesh.
certificate_summary.theorem_level_A: Level A (pointwise mesh): For every gamma_i in the certified mesh (|Gamma| = 118), Krawczyk certifies a unique nondegenerate root of F_tilde(., gamma_i) = 0 in X_i, with divisor separation on X_i. Certificate type: discrete_gamma_points. Mesh uses code_gamma_negative_seed_chamber; do not read as 0 < gamma <= gamma_{-2pi} in physical positive coordinates without declaring physical_gamma_positive_with_gamma_code_equals_minus_gamma.
certificate_summary.theorem_level_B: Level B (mesh extension of analytic LOC): Together with the analytic LOC certificate near gamma = 0 (Thm 6.1 / Banach radius), the pointwise Krawczyk certificates (discrete_gamma_points) extend the verified BM24 seed branch on the sampled mesh beyond the analytic contraction radius.
